minutes.headline: Committee tabled the FY22 school choice vote and heard FY22 budget updates on Chapter 70, health insurance and new grants.
minutes.summary: The committee approved a primary school line item transfer and the January 20th minutes, then tabled the FY22 school choice seat decision until more information is available. The business manager reported updates since the proposed FY22 budget: a health insurance premium holiday, a small Chapter 70 increase, and two new grants. A budget Q&A drew few questions, followed by reports and an executive session on union negotiations.

what_happened.line: The School Committee tabled the FY22 school choice seat decision to a future meeting, 5-0, pending testing results and state guidance.
The business manager reported a health insurance premium holiday, a Chapter 70 increase smaller than the statewide percent, and new grants since the proposed FY22 budget.
The committee approved, 5-0, a transfer at the primary school from band and music supplies to general supplies.
Administration is to provide an adjusted FY22 budget on February 24th, with another budget Q&A on March 3rd.
A resident said the agenda was not on the town website calendar; the chair said it was posted at town hall, so no open meeting law issue.

why_it_matters: School choice seats bring in tuition revenue, and the superintendent said staying out long term would shift costs now paid from that account onto the local budget, which is mostly taxes.
The size of the Chapter 70 increase and the one-time premium holiday help set how much of the FY22 school budget the town must cover, which feeds into the tax bill and the Town Meeting vote.
watch_next: February 24th: the adjusted FY22 school budget from administration.
March 3rd: the next FY22 budget Q&A, and the tabled school choice vote at a future meeting.
